step.name: Step 1: Initial Consultation and Design Development
step.text: This phase involves defining your functional requirements and budget, then creating detailed designs. This back-and-forth ensures your vision is perfectly captured and might take a few weeks depending on design complexity and your feedback.

step.name: Step 2: Material and Hardware Selection
step.text: You'll choose your wood type, finishes, door styles, and hardware. The availability of these specific selections can influence the overall timeline, as some specialty items may have longer lead times.

step.name: Step 3: Field Verification and Shop Drawings
step.text: Precise field measurements are taken at your home, and detailed shop drawings are created for your approval. This step is crucial for ensuring everything fits perfectly and preventing costly mistakes.

step.name: Step 4: Customer Approval and Production Scheduling
step.text: Once you approve the final drawings, the project moves into the production queue. This is when the actual manufacturing lead time begins, typically reported to be in the 6-12 week range for fabrication.

step.name: Step 5: Production and Inspection
step.text: During this phase, your cabinets are meticulously crafted. After fabrication, they undergo thorough inspection to ensure quality and adherence to specifications.

step.name: Step 6: Delivery and Installation
step.text: Once produced and inspected, your custom cabinets are delivered to your home and expertly installed. This final step brings your vision to life. Understanding these phases helps you appreciate why custom cabinetry isn't an overnight process. It’s a thoughtful journey to create something truly unique and perfectly fitted for your home. LineWork Development believes in transparent communication throughout this process, ensuring you’re always in the loop.
